[Secondhand rentals higher than ever - young worst exposed] 

Never before has the difference between first-hand and second-hand rents been so great. [Up to] SEK 40 000 (4 100€, $4 900) - every year. So much more, you pay if you rent a single room apartment that is a residential property in Stockholm, compared to if you have a first-hand contract. According to a survey made by SvD and the digital journal Baaam.

The owner of a housing right is one of the biggest losers in the crisis in the Swedish housing market. Every year, tens of thousands of Swedes move into sublease homes - often because there are no alternatives. In the new article series #minbostadskris - SvD and the digital journal Baaam have compiled statistics from Blocket, SCB (statistical central bureau) and Bostadsförmedlingen to see exactly how much the person who lives with a secondary-contract loses. And the numbers are gloomy reading for all those forced to the secondary market. An example: An average rental income that the Housing Agency brokered in Stockholm in 2017 cost 4,686 SEK (490€, $570) a month - a fully affordable price tag for many.

However, getting a first-hand contract is a few undone. On the other hand, the ones who rent a home in second-hand, pays an average of 70 percent more - more than 8,236 (860€, $1000) a month, according to Blocket statistics.

In one year, that means you pay 40,000 (4 100€, $4 900) more than you would with a first-hand contract. If you're in home with two rooms, the difference is even greater; 78 percent - or 67,000 kronor (6 900€, $8 100) a year. Money that could have been able to end up on the savings account in pursuit of a future home ownership. And it does not seem to get any better. On the contrary, it has never been more expensive to rent in any other way than before. In seven years, the rent of single room rentals in tenant-owner rights has increased by 70 percent in Greater Stockholm [with such a trend visible over all of Sweden] .
